key_insight: MathNet delivers a high-quality, large-scale, multimodal and multilingual benchmark of Olympiad-level math problems that evaluates both generative mathematical reasoning and embedding-based mathematical retrieval in a single unified suite.
problem_solved: Existing benchmarks are small, narrowly scoped, and lack language and modality diversity, making it hard to evaluate models on realistic, high-difficulty mathematical reasoning and cross-modal/multilingual retrieval tasks.
method: Curate a large corpus of Olympiad-level math problems spanning 47 countries and 17 languages, preserving multimodal content (text, equations, diagrams/images).

Define two evaluation tracks: (1) generative mathematical reasoning for LLMs and multimodal models, and (2) embedding-based mathematical retrieval for similarity and search systems, with standardized splits and metrics.
Provide preprocessing and task interfaces that convert problems into multimodal inputs and retrieval targets to support both generation and embedding workflows.
impact: MathNet enables more robust, fair, and realistic evaluation of advanced reasoning and retrieval models across languages and modalities, accelerating development of models that can handle challenging mathematical content in global contexts.
visual_elements: World map highlighting the 47 contributing countries with callouts for language coverage (17 languages).
Pipeline diagram showing dataset ingestion → multimodal formatting → two benchmark tracks (generative reasoning vs embedding retrieval).
Stacked bar or pie chart of modality composition (text, LaTeX/equations, diagrams/images) and problem difficulty distribution.
Example problem card: original multimodal problem (image + LaTeX) alongside a model's generated solution snippet and retrieval neighbors.
paper_title: MathNet: a Global Multimodal Benchmark for Mathematical Reasoning and Retrieval
paper_authors: Shaden Alshammari, Kevin Wen, Abrar Zainal, Mark Hamilton, Navid Safaei
